title: Introduce tenant cost-governor and quantization interop shim
author: Maya Singh
release_notes: Adds tenant-scoped cost-governor that synthesizes batching/caching defaults and a lightweight quantization compatibility shim to avoid runtime fallbacks.
body: Motivation: Customers operating many tenants hit two correlated pain points: (1) conservative global defaults that underutilize batching/caching opportunities per-tenant; (2) expensive runtime fallbacks when quantization profile mismatches occur between model variants. This PR introduces a tenant cost-governor service and a quantization interop shim to automatically propose safe defaults and ensure compatibility between quantized model variants. Summary of changes: tenant cost-governor service that ingests tenant profile (traffic shape, latency SLO, budget band) and emits recommended batching, prefix-cache, and quant presets; quantization interop shim that negotiates a lowest-risk quant profile at routing time, producing a deterministic compatibility mapping and a lightweight fallback plan instead of immediate downgrade to dense variants; CLI preview tool redwood cost-preview to dry-run recommendations against replayed traces; telemetry hooks to surface unit-econ delta per-tenant and a new metric tenant.cost_governor.suggested_defaults.applied_ratio. Safety: new feature-gate defaulted off; rollout via canary to 5% tenants then 50% then 100% with automatic rollback on quality regressions. Tests & results: unit tests added for governor algorithm, integration tests between router and shim, end-to-end synthetic workload showing 7-12% token-cost reduction and negligible median p95 latency impact (+3ms) for our bench tenant sample. Backwards compatibility: shim falls back to existing routing behavior when no compatible quant mapping is found. Migration: lightweight tenant schema (v1) plus a migration command which backfills tenant profiles from historical telemetry. Checklist: [x] design doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-8132/tenant-cost-governor-design [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] perf baseline [x] feature-flag + rollout plan [x] docs stub. Commits and changed areas listed below. Merge strategy: squash-and-merge after approvals and CI green.

review_comments: Liam Carter: Overall looks good; main concern is ensuring mapping_builder complexity stays O(n) and doesn't add jitter to router path.
Maya Singh (author): mapping_builder precomputes compatibility buckets asynchronously; router consults a constant-time lookup cache; added tests to prove latency invariants.
Sofia Alvarez: Add a probe for quant-quality regression detection and link to existing eval hooks.
Maya Singh (author): wired in eval-hook webhook; governor will block auto-apply if eval-hook reports regression beyond threshold.
Jordan Kim: Need an escape hatch in the feature flag for tenants with strict SLOs; suggest tag-based opt-out.
Maya Singh (author): implemented tenant tag opt-out and updated rollout docs.
